_note: US English — the source of truth. To add a language, copy this file to data/i18n/<code>.json, translate the values (never the keys), and add the locale to LOCALES in site/js/i18n.js. Anything you leave out falls back to this file, so a partial translation is safe to ship.

app.name: Nightlight
app.description: County-level drug supply alerts, drug-checking results, and how to test a supply. Harm reduction information, not medical advice.

theme.light: Light theme is on. Switch to dark.
theme.dark: Dark theme is on. Switch to light.

app.quickExit: Leave now — clears what is on this device, overwrites the back button, and leaves this site
app.loadFailedHint: Check your connection and try again.
app.earlyTitle: Early access — tell us if something here is wrong
app.earlyBody: Some of this may be wrong. Every clinical claim is checked against a source prior to you seeing it, but we still may have made mistakes. If you see anything wrong, especially something that could hurt someone, please reach out:
app.earlyBanner: Early access — some of this may be wrong.

footer.disclaimerLead: This is information, not medical advice.
footer.disclaimerBody: Nightlight reports what public sources published. It does not verify, advise, or clear any drug as safe. No test, and no absence of alerts, makes a supply safe.
footer.emergency: Overdose is a medical emergency — call
footer.privacy: We do not save or sell any of your data. ✕ clears this device and overwrites the back button. A private window is the only way to leave no trace, as we cannot erase your browser history.

alerts.heading: What's showing up near you
alerts.intro: Warnings published by health departments, local reporting, and drug-checking labs — for your county and the ones around it. Supply moves across county lines, so both matter. Search a city or a county to start.
alerts.searchLabel: Search for a city or county
alerts.searchPlaceholder: Search your city or county — Chattanooga, Multnomah…
alerts.locationPrivacyTitle: Your location never leaves this device
alerts.locationPrivacyBody: “Near me” works out your county inside this browser, using map data that came down with the page. Nothing is asked of a location service, and your coordinates are never sent anywhere.
alerts.noScanBody: Once the hourly job runs, alerts will appear here. Until then this page has nothing to report — which is not the same as nothing happening.
alerts.borderingIntro: Supply moves across county lines. These are the counties that touch {county}, nearest first.
alerts.notHereTitle: Nothing published for {county} in the last {window}
alerts.notHereBody: This does not mean the supply here is safe. Most changes in a local drug supply are never publicly announced, and reporting runs behind reality by weeks. Treat this as “no information”, not “no risk”.
alerts.notHereNearby: There are {count} alerts in bordering counties — see below.
alerts.unknownCounty: That county code isn’t one we have.
alerts.unknownCountyHint: Search for a county by name instead.
alerts.locating: Asking your browser for a location…
alerts.locatingMatch: Matching coordinates to a county on this device…
alerts.locateFound: Found {county}. Your coordinates stayed on this device.
alerts.locateDenied: Location permission denied. Search by name instead.
alerts.locateTimeout: Location timed out. Try again, or search by name.
alerts.locateFailed: Couldn’t get a location. Search by name instead.
alerts.locateUnsupported: This browser can’t share location. Search by name instead.
alerts.locateOutside: That location isn’t inside a US county. Search by name instead.
alerts.locateNoData: Couldn’t load the map data. Search by name instead.
alerts.sessionTitle: Nothing you do here is saved
alerts.sessionBody: No account, and nothing kept between visits — close the tab and it is gone. The ✕ in the corner is for when you need to leave this second: it clears what this site stored, walks the back button back over where you have been, and sends you to a weather site. What it cannot do is erase the browser's own history — for that, use a private window.
alerts.everywhereIntro: Every alert published anywhere in the country, newest and most serious first.
alerts.everywhereCount: {count} published anywhere in the country in the last {window}.
alerts.everywhereNoneTitle: Nothing published anywhere in the last {window}
alerts.everywhereNoneBody: That says what has been published, not what is going around. Most changes in a local drug supply are never announced by anyone, and the reporting that does happen runs weeks behind. A quiet list means nobody has said anything — not that nothing is happening.
alerts.everywhereNoneScanned: We have looked at {count} counties recently, out of 3,231. Most of the country has not been looked at at all.

map.metricChangeHint: Overdose deaths compared with the same 12 months a year earlier. Independent of population.
map.metricDeathsHint: Overdose deaths in the last 12 months. This largely tracks population — big counties are tall because they are big.
map.metricAlertsHint: Supply alerts published in the selected window.
map.canvasLabel: Three-dimensional map of US counties. Height shows change in overdose deaths. Use the county list below this map, or the search box, to open a county — the map itself is a visual summary.
map.help: Drag to turn. Scroll or pinch to zoom. Tap a county to open it.
map.noFigure: Counties with no shading have no published figure. Counts of 1–9 are withheld for confidentiality, so blank is not the same as none.
map.noAlertsBody: The scanner works through all 3,231 counties over about a week, and genuine supply advisories are rare in any given hour. Nothing has qualified so far.
map.noAlertsMeaning: This is an absence of reporting, not evidence of a safe supply. Try “Change vs last year”, which has data for every county with a published figure.
map.noDataTitle: No figures available for this measure
map.noDataBody: Nothing to map yet. Try another measure.

content.title: Some of this page is only in English
content.body: The clinical guidance below has not been translated yet. Nothing has been left out of the English version.
content.lines: The crisis lines in the footer answer in Spanish as well as English.
